sentences.text: Why do traffic jams appear out of nowhere?
In two thousand eight, researchers in Japan put twenty-two cars on a circular track.
No lights, no crashes. Just drive at a steady thirty kilometers an hour.
One driver eased off a little, the next braked a bit harder, and so on.
The wave grew into a full stop that crept backward around the track.
So when cars are packed too close, traffic can jam all by itself.
